newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber boosted by reports of Thai buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber boosted by reports of Thai buying.

text.p: Singapore rubber prices were given a boost on Wednesday by rumours that the Thai government was said to have bought up to 5,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber, dealers said.
"There was a rumour the Thai government bought 5,000 tonnes at around 123.00-124.00 U.S. cents (a kg)," a senior trader for a rubber trading house here said.

"That will not be surprising," a dealer for a North American trading house said when asked about the purchase. But even if the purchase was true, "it will only help the market over the short-term because demand is really so weak," the dealer added.
Singapore-based traders estimate the Thai government has bought around 13,000-14,000 tonnes since it announced a policy of supporting rubber prices.
Business in the rubber trade remained slow, dealers said. "There's not really much going on in the market at the moment," a senior dealer said.

At around 0930 GMT, May RSS3 was seen at 121.00-123.00 U.S. cents a kg from 122.00 cents. May RSS1 was indicated unchanged at 174.50 Singapore cents (US$1.22) a kg. May TSR20 was seen at 162.50-164.50 Singapore cents (US$1.13-$1.15) a kg from 163.50 cents. - (US$1-S$1.43) - Rene Pastor (65-8703305)
